title: Download on a constrained device
blurb: Reads live device hints (navigator.connection, Save-Data, deviceMemory, storage.estimate, navigator.onLine) alongside Translator.availability() to advise whether to translate, ask first, or wait for Wi-Fi, with consent-gated create(), downloadprogress, cancel, and destroy().
question: How can a mobile web app combine network, memory, and storage hints with Translator.availability() to gate language-pack downloads behind explicit user consent with progress, cancellation, and cleanup?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux), live device signals drove the download decision and pressing Cancel during Translator.create() produced AbortError (no downloadprogress events arrived within 3 s in the sandbox). Completed pack download and constrained-network (3G / Save-Data) paths not verified on Chrome for Android 161.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux, decision and cancel verified); not verified on Chrome for Android 161

friction.summary: Pages cannot read language-pack download sizes or free space in Chrome's shared model store before calling Translator.create()
friction.repro: Inspect navigator.storage.estimate() and Translator.availability(); estimate() reflects origin quota rather than the browser model store, and availability() exposes no byte size.
friction.workaround: Combine navigator.connection (saveData, effectiveType, type) and deviceMemory as conservative hints, never auto-download, attach an AbortSignal + downloadprogress monitor, and handle NetworkError/NotSupportedError explicitly.
